description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-api/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md) and the store specs admin-access ('Database not published') and content-authoring (CA-D21). Pay attention to: tools/stack.mjs --check-bind accepting anything outside loopback/RFC 1918 (IPv6 forms, IPv4-mapped, leading zeros, hostnames, 0.0.0.0 spellings); compose.yaml ports that bypass DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS; backup/restore writing inside a repository, leaking the DB password on the command line or in logs, or restore destroying data without a guard; any path where request body, query or headers reach logs (filters, actuator httpexchanges, Spring debug settings); the security config leaving /api/admin/** or actuator endpoints open; undeclared paths returning anything other than problem+json without driver internals; FixtureProvenanceTest missing fixture roots; the Dockerfile and .dockerignore copying .env or secrets; the .editorconfig ktlint package-name rule disabled. Also review the DNS-rebinding fix (commit 5bf3df9): the StrictHttpFirewall host allowlist (localhost, bare IPv4, backend) and its 400 problem+json, and compose.yaml no longer publishing the backend port. Report only defects in shipped behaviour or tests that can pass while the spec is violated by ordinary use.

findings.title: Actuator discovery root /actuator stays exposed and answers 200 HAL JSON, not 404 problem+json
findings.evidence: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health` limits which endpoints are exposed, but it leaves `management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled` at its default (true). So `GET /actuator` returns 200 with an `application/vnd.spring-boot.actuator.v3+json` `_links` document. The spec says only the health endpoint is exposed and that any undeclared path is 404 problem+json. The IT test `only the health endpoint of actuator is reachable` checks only /actuator/modulith, /info, /env and /httpexchanges, so it passes while this violation ships. Similar gap: /actuator/health/<component> is refused by actuator itself with an empty-body 404, not problem+json.
findings.suggestion: Set `management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled: false`. Add `/actuator` (and e.g. `/actuator/health/db`) to the IT test, and check the problem+json content type and catalog title as well as the status.

findings.title: FixtureProvenanceTest exempts docs/qa/ wholesale, so screenshots or PDFs there skip the 'any media file anywhere in git' rule
findings.evidence: `val OUT_OF_SCOPE = listOf("contract/", "target/", "node_modules/", "docs/qa/")` is checked first in `inScope`, so `docs/qa/evidence/page.png` returns false before the MEDIA rule runs. The spec delta puts in scope "every image, document, audio or video file anywhere in git" and lists no docs/qa exemption. QA evidence screenshots are exactly where workbook pages or the child's data (NFR-3/NFR-4) would end up, and the test stays green.
findings.suggestion: Remove `docs/qa/` from OUT_OF_SCOPE, or apply only the MEDIA rule to it. Add a case such as `docs/qa/evidence/shot.png` to the negative test.

findings.title: git ls-files output is C-quoted for non-ASCII names, so Czech-named fixtures are silently dropped from the provenance check
findings.evidence: `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` prints names with non-ASCII bytes as `"fixtures/\303\272loha.png"` under the default `core.quotePath=true`. `gitFiles()` then applies `out.filter { File(it).isFile }`, which drops those quoted strings because no such file exists. A file named with Czech diacritics (e.g. `úloha.pdf`) is never checked, and the test passes with workbook content committed.
findings.suggestion: Run `git -c core.quotePath=false ls-files -z ...` and split on NUL. Fail, rather than filter, when a listed path does not exist on disk.

findings.title: Migration 'pure DDL' exemption only spots INSERT/COPY/UPDATE at line start
findings.evidence: `Regex("""(?im)^\s*(insert|copy|update)\b""")` misses data written as `CREATE TABLE t(x text); INSERT INTO t ...` on one line, `WITH s AS (...) INSERT ...`, `MERGE`, and `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT/VALUES`. A seed migration written in any of these forms counts as exempt DDL, so answer keys can enter a migration without a provenance row.
findings.suggestion: Match the data keywords at any statement boundary (`(^|;)\s*(with|insert|copy|update|merge)\b`) and also look for `VALUES`/`AS SELECT`. Simpler: treat every migration as in scope unless it is explicitly allowlisted.

findings.title: Tomcat logs the raw request target (query string included) at INFO when a request line has an invalid character, and the INFO cap does not stop it
findings.evidence: The guard denies only levels below INFO for `org.apache.coyote`. When a query contains characters outside Tomcat's relaxedQueryChars, Tomcat's Http11Processor logs `Error parsing HTTP request header` at INFO for the first occurrence. Browsers leave `{`, `|` and `}` unencoded in queries. The nested IllegalArgumentException message `Invalid character found in the request target [...]` contains the target and its query. That puts request content in the log at the configured level (NFR-3). The same request also gets Tomcat's own 400 rather than problem+json. The tests use MockMvc and a well-formed HttpClient, so they never exercise this path.
findings.suggestion: Cap `org.apache.coyote.http11` (or all of `org.apache.coyote`) at WARN in the guard, or set `org.apache.juli.logging.UserDataHelper.CONFIG=NONE`. Add a raw-socket IT case that sends a sentinel in an invalid query and checks it does not appear in CapturedOutput.

findings.title: JDBC bind-value logger of Spring JDBC not covered by the guard
findings.evidence: GUARDED covers Hibernate's `org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind` and `org.postgresql`. It does not cover `org.springframework.jdbc`, whose `StatementCreatorUtils` logs every bound parameter value at TRACE (`Setting SQL statement parameter value: ... parameter value [...]`). The spec says the 'Hibernate/JDBC bind values' loggers are capped. Any JdbcTemplate/JdbcClient use (including in later slices) would log answers at TRACE, and the TRACE test, which never touches the database, cannot catch it.

findings.title: FixtureProvenanceTest skips every file under docs/qa/, so screenshots and recordings can be committed there without failing the check
findings.evidence: The spec delta covers 'every image, document, audio or video file anywhere in git', but `OUT_OF_SCOPE` contains "docs/qa/". `inScope()` returns false for those paths before it ever reaches the `MEDIA` check. docs/qa/evidence/ is where this harness writes slice evidence (slice1-compose-smoke.md, review-fixes). Suppose an agent or developer saves a UI screenshot there, e.g. docs/qa/evidence/slice2-practice.png showing a workbook page or the child's name. The provenance test stays green and the CA-D21 / NFR-3 / NFR-4 guard is bypassed in exactly the folder where screenshots are most likely to be saved.
findings.suggestion: Exempt only the generated text reports under docs/qa (for example *.md, *.json and *.jsonl there). Keep the MEDIA rule for every path except contract/, target/ and node_modules/. Add a case with `docs/qa/evidence/shot.png` to the 'unlisted fixture … fails' test.

findings.title: Tomcat logs a rejected request target, query string included, at INFO, which the log guard lets through
findings.evidence: The guard only drops events below INFO (`!level.isGreaterOrEqual(Level.INFO)`). Tomcat's Http11Processor logs the first request-line parse failure in each suppression window at INFO, as 'Error parsing HTTP request header … Invalid character found in the request target [<path>?<query>]'. The WHATWG URL rules do not percent-encode `{ } | ^ \ `` ` in a query, so a browser fetch such as `?answer=a|b` from the child UI, or a request from any LAN client, puts the raw query value in the backend log. RequestContentNotLoggedTest only sends a sentinel made of legal characters, so it passes while this NFR-3 path stays open. The response is also Tomcat's own 400 rather than problem+json.
findings.suggestion: Cap org.apache.coyote.http11.Http11Processor (or all org.apache.coyote) at WARN in the guard, or set `server.tomcat.relaxed-query-chars` and handle the input in the app. Add a raw-socket test case that sends a sentinel containing `|` in the query and asserts the captured output does not contain it.

findings.title: The provenance test's scope classifiers miss common document types and data-bearing migrations
findings.evidence: `DATA_STATEMENT` only matches `insert|copy|update` at the start of a line. A seed migration written as `WITH s AS (...) INSERT INTO task ...`, `MERGE INTO …`, `DO $$ BEGIN INSERT …`, or `CREATE TABLE …; INSERT …` on one line is treated as pure DDL and exempted, so workbook task text or answer keys in a Flyway migration pass the CA-D21 check. Outside src/ and fixtures/, `MEDIA` (line 21) also misses document and archive formats such as rtf, pptx/odp, epub, djvu, zip and the backup format `.dump`. A `git add -f` of a backup or a workbook archive therefore goes unflagged.
findings.suggestion: Match data statements anywhere in a statement, e.g. `(?i)\b(insert\s+into|copy\s+\w+\s+from|merge\s+into|update\s+\w+\s+set)\b`. Extend MEDIA with rtf, pptx, ppt, odp, epub, djvu, zip, 7z and dump. Add both to the negative test.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 21 scenarios: 18 implemented, 3 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted
findings.evidence: Checked 16 delta scenarios, plus admin-access 'Local network only' (3: Default binding is loopback, Configured LAN address, Database not published) and content-authoring CA-D21 (2). Implemented: bind checks (BindAddressTest, tools/lib/compose.mjs:33-42, publishedPortProblems uses `docker compose config`), compose ports (only frontend publishes, on ${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}; db and backend publish nothing), backup/restore (BackupRestoreIT, 4 tests; OperatorToolGuardTest, 3 tests), admin 403, undeclared 404, firewall 400, no generated password, actuator 404s. Partial: Container-level errors, Nothing leaks even at TRACE / configured levels, Every fixture has a self-authored provenance entry (see the findings below). No password on any command line (restore and backup use `docker compose exec` without credentials); the Dockerfile COPYs only pom/.mvn/contract/api/src/main, and .dockerignore excludes **/.env*. The ktlint package-name rule is turned off only under adapter/in/**.
findings.suggestion: No action. This entry is the coverage summary.

findings.title: Tomcat-level URL rejections bypass the problem+json path, and Tomcat logs the raw request target at INFO, which the log guard lets through
findings.evidence: Spec: 'A request to a path the contract does not declare SHALL be answered 404 ... problem+json ... A URL the security firewall rejects SHALL be answered 400 problem+json' and 'No request body, query-string or header value SHALL appear in the backend's logs at any log level'. Code: the guard only denies events below INFO (`!level.isGreaterOrEqual(Level.INFO)`) for org.apache.coyote/catalina/tomcat. Tomcat rejects some request targets in the connector, before Spring Security or MVC run: raw `|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `[`, `]`, `\` in the query or path, and encoded `%2F`/`%5C`. Browsers do not percent-encode `|{}^[]\` in query strings, and nginx forwards the request line unchanged. For these requests Tomcat answers with its own ErrorReportValve HTML 400, not problem+json from the catalog. Http11Processor also logs 'Error parsing HTTP request header … Invalid character found in the request target [<target incl. query>]' at INFO (the first occurrence, then DEBUG via UserDataHelper). An INFO line passes the guard, so query content reaches the log. RequestContentNotLoggedTest and UndeclaredPathTest use MockMvc only, and the real-port IT covers only `//`, `;` and `%2e%2e`. Tests can therefore pass while this path breaks the spec.
findings.suggestion: Add a real-port test that sends a raw request with `?q=a|SENTINEL` and with `%2F` in the path. Assert that the response is problem+json and that the sentinel is not in the captured output. Then fix it: set Tomcat's UserDataHelper log mode to quiet (`org.apache.tomcat.util.http.parser` / `-Dorg.apache.juli.logging.UserDataHelper.CONFIG=NONE`), or cap org.apache.coyote.http11 at WARN, and set `server.tomcat.relaxed-query-chars` / relaxed-path-chars (or a custom ErrorReportValve) so these requests reach the problem+json writer. If any case stays out of scope, amend the spec to say so.

findings.title: FixtureProvenanceTest exempts all of docs/qa/, but the spec covers every image, document, audio or video file anywhere in git
findings.evidence: Spec delta: 'In scope: ... every image, document, audio or video file anywhere in git. Exempt: application.yaml, logback-spring.xml, the message catalog, and Flyway migrations without data statements'. CA-D21: 'exits non-zero for any fixture file that is missing from the manifest'. Code: `val OUT_OF_SCOPE = listOf("contract/", "target/", "node_modules/", "docs/qa/")`, and inScope returns false for these prefixes before the MEDIA check. A screenshot or PDF committed under docs/qa/ (the evidence directory, where screenshots are most likely to land) passes the check. That is exactly the NFR-4/NFR-3 leak the check exists to catch, and the spec lists no such exemption. A smaller gap: DATA_STATEMENT `^\s*(insert|copy|update)\b` misses `MERGE` and CTE-prefixed `WITH … INSERT` seed migrations, so they count as pure DDL and are exempt.
findings.suggestion: Remove docs/qa/ from OUT_OF_SCOPE for MEDIA files, or keep it only for non-media files. If evidence media must be allowed, amend the spec and still require manifest rows for them. Add `merge` and `with` to DATA_STATEMENT, and add the matching cases to the 'unlisted fixture' test.

findings.title: The DNS-rebinding Host allowlist and the unpublished backend port have no backing requirement in the spec delta
findings.evidence: Commit 5bf3df9 adds `setAllowedHostnames { host -> host == "localhost" || host == "backend" || IPV4.matches(host) }`, which answers any other Host with 400 problem+json, and it stops publishing the backend port (compose.yaml, the backend service has no `ports`). This behaviour is user-visible: a LAN client that uses an mDNS or hostname URL gets a 400, and the API is reachable only through the frontend's nginx. It is recorded only in design.md decision 2a and the tasks.md 4.4 note. The spec delta still only says 'A URL the security firewall rejects SHALL be answered 400 problem+json' and has no requirement or scenario for a Host allowlist or for the backend staying unpublished. Also, IPV4 = `\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}` accepts any dotted quad, including 999.1.1.1 and public addresses. That is harmless against rebinding but is not what the KDoc says ('loopback or the LAN address').
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec delta, and the store admin-access spec through a docs-store change. Add a 'Foreign Host refused' requirement with the scenarios already tested in DouckoBackendApplicationIT (evil.example → 400 problem+json; localhost, 127.0.0.1, backend:8080 accepted), and a 'Backend port not published' scenario. Align the KDoc with the regex, or tighten the regex.

findings.title: /actuator discovery root is still exposed although the spec says only health is
findings.evidence: Spec: 'Only the actuator health endpoint SHALL be exposed.' Code: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health`. Boot's links endpoint `/actuator` stays enabled by default (management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled=true), so it answers 200 with `_links`. The IT checks only modulith/info/env/httpexchanges, so `/actuator` is never tested.
findings.suggestion: Set `management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled: false` and add `/actuator` to the 404 list in DouckoBackendApplicationIT. Otherwise amend the spec to allow the discovery page.

findings.title: Task 4.4 smoke is ticked, but its evidence predates the compose change and uses the now-unpublished port 8080
findings.evidence: Task 4.4 [x]: 'curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health → UP; curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/child/nope'. Evidence: docs/qa/evidence/slice1-compose-smoke.md, last touched in f553d30, before 5bf3df9. 5bf3df9 removed the backend's published port, and the added note only says 'a re-run of this smoke goes through the frontend'. Nothing shows that re-run happened, so the ticked smoke does not describe the configuration that ships (done-claims-need-evidence).
findings.suggestion: Re-run the smoke through 127.0.0.1:8081: `docker compose ps` should show only 127.0.0.1:8081 and healthy backend/db, and curl through nginx should return the 404 problem+json and the Host 400. Update slice1-compose-smoke.md, or untick 4.4 until that is done.

result.reasoning: I could not refute the mechanism. In application.yaml (lines 40-45), `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health` is the only actuator setting, so `management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled` keeps its default of true. Nothing else blocks `/actuator`: SecurityConfiguration only denies `/api/admin/**` and permits every other request, and the StrictHttpFirewall only checks the Host header. A request to `GET /actuator` from localhost or a LAN IP therefore reaches Actuator's discovery handler and gets 200 with a HAL `_links` document (self, health, health-path). The IT test `only the health endpoint of actuator is reachable` (DouckoBackendApplicationIT.kt:92-97) never requests `/actuator` and only checks the status code, so it can't catch this. The change spec (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-api/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md:13) says "Only the actuator health endpoint SHALL be exposed", and design.md:95 says any undeclared path gets 404 problem+json. The discovery root breaks both. The health/<component> point is also plausible: by default Actuator refuses an unshown component itself with a bare 404 and no body, so the problem+json mapping never runs. I didn't run the app to confirm that part. Severity: the discovery page only reveals links to health, which is already public, so nothing sensitive is exposed. This is a real spec and contract gap, but its security impact is low. I'd downgrade it from major to minor.

I confirmed the mechanism, but it does very little harm.

**What the code shows**
- `application.yaml:40-45` sets only `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health`. It never sets `management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled`, so Spring Boot's default (`true`) applies.
- `SecurityConfiguration.kt:65-67` does `authorize("/api/admin/**", denyAll)` and then `authorize(anyRequest, permitAll)`. Nothing in security or any filter blocks `/actuator`.
- With discovery left on and at least one endpoint exposed, Boot's `WebMvcEndpointHandlerMapping` registers the links handler at the base path. `GET /actuator` therefore returns 200 with `application/vnd.spring-boot.actuator.v3+json` and `_links` (`self`, `health`, `health-path`). It does not reach MVC's `NoResourceFoundException` path, which is the one that produces the catalog-titled 404 problem+json.
- The comment at `SecurityConfiguration.kt:25` promises "an undeclared path is 404 problem+json", so this is a real deviation from the stated contract.
- The IT test at `DouckoBackendApplicationIT.kt:92-94` checks only `/modulith`, `/info`, `/env` and `/httpexchanges`, so the test-coverage gap is real too.
- The `/actuator/health/<component>` point also holds. With the default `show-components` setting, actuator's health endpoint returns its own empty-body 404, not problem+json.

**Limits**
- I did not run the app; the Testcontainers IT needs Docker. The conclusion rests on reading the code plus Spring Boot's documented default for discovery.

**Exploitability**
- Anyone on the LAN can reproduce it with one GET.
- All it reveals is the actuator base path and the health link. The compose healthcheck already uses that path and it carries no sensitive data.
- No other endpoint becomes reachable, and NFR-2's intent (only health reachable) still holds in substance.

So this is a valid spec-conformance and test-coverage defect, not a security exposure. "major" overstates it; minor fits better. The fix is still cheap and correct: set `discovery.enabled: false`, and add `/actuator` and `/actuator/health/db` to the IT with content-type and title assertions.

I confirmed the finding. The pattern at FixtureProvenanceTest.kt:25 is `(?im)^\s*(insert|copy|update)\b`. Because of the `m` flag, `^` matches only at the start of a line. That means:
- `CREATE TABLE t(x text); INSERT INTO t VALUES ...` written on one line does not match: INSERT comes after `;`, not at the start of the line.
- `MERGE INTO ...` does not match at all.
- `CREATE TABLE t AS VALUES/SELECT ...` does not match.
- `WITH s AS (...) INSERT ...` on one line does not match.

At line 36, `inScope` returns false for a migration whose content doesn't match. Such a migration is treated as exempt DDL, so line 72 never asks for a manifest row.

Nothing else covers this gap: the .githooks have no migration or INSERT check, and the unit test at line 110 only covers the case where INSERT starts a line.

This is only a heuristic gap in a test-time guard, and the attack needs an unusually written seed migration, so "minor" is the right severity.

The mechanism is real. At FixtureProvenanceTest.kt:36, a Flyway migration counts as in scope only when `DATA_STATEMENT.containsMatchIn(...)` finds a match. The pattern `(?im)^\s*(insert|copy|update)\b` matches only when the keyword starts a line, apart from leading whitespace. Each of these would be treated as exempt pure DDL, so no provenance row would be required:
- `CREATE TABLE t(x text); INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)` on one line (after `;` the next character is a space, not a line start)
- `WITH s AS (...) INSERT ...` on one line
- `MERGE INTO ...`
- `CREATE TABLE t AS VALUES/SELECT ...`
- `INSERT` written after a block comment on the same line

Nothing else guards this. No other check scans migration content, and the unit test (line 110) only covers the case where INSERT starts a line. The only migration file today is `.gitkeep`, so nothing slips through yet. But this is a guard for future seed migrations, and a single-line CTE or MERGE seed is a realistic way to write one.

On exploitability: this is a developer-process control for NFR-4 / CA-D21, not something a runtime attacker can reach. The bypass would happen by accident or carelessness, not as an attack. - **No child endpoint takes a query parameter.** In `contract/api/openapi.yaml` the only `in: query` parameters are on admin-session endpoints: task list filters including `q`, preview `locale`, stats `weeks` and flag-queue `status`. Answers are not sent in a query, so the claimed browser fetch `?answer=a|b` from the child UI does not exist in this API.
- **None of these values is child PII.** The only free-text parameter is the admin's search `q` over Czech task prompts, and the rest are enums or integers. NFR-3 is about the child's personal data.
- **The "any LAN client" case leaks nothing.** That client can only get its own chosen bytes into the log. That is self-injection, not exposure of someone else's data.
- **Real clients encode these characters.** Clients built with URLSearchParams, encodeURIComponent or a generated client percent-encode `| { } ^ \ \``. A raw `|` only reaches Tomcat if someone hand-concatenates a URL or uses a raw socket.
- **The 400 being Tomcat's own response rather than problem+json** concerns malformed request lines that never reach the app. It is not part of NFR-3.

Limits of this check: I could not open the frontend source or the local Tomcat jar (permission was denied), so I did not confirm the frontend's encoding or Tomcat's exact message text.

Optionally capping Http11Processor at WARN would be a small hardening step. It is not an NFR-3 leak a real user or attacker could use.

rejected.title: JDBC bind-value logger of Spring JDBC not covered by the guard
rejected.evidence: GUARDED covers Hibernate's `org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind` and `org.postgresql`. It does not cover `org.springframework.jdbc`, whose `StatementCreatorUtils` logs every bound parameter value at TRACE (`Setting SQL statement parameter value: ... parameter value [...]`). The spec says the 'Hibernate/JDBC bind values' loggers are capped. Any JdbcTemplate/JdbcClient use (including in later slices) would log answers at TRACE, and the TRACE test, which never touches the database, cannot catch it.
verifierNotes: The guard list at RequestContentLogGuard.kt:34-47 is quoted correctly: it doesn't include `org.springframework.jdbc`. spring-jdbc is on the classpath through spring-boot-starter-data-jpa. But no code path in this repo reaches `StatementCreatorUtils`. A search for JdbcTemplate, JdbcClient and NamedParameterJdbc across the repo found nothing. Persistence goes through Spring Data JPA/Hibernate, which binds parameters with its own binders and logs them under `org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind` and `org.hibernate.type`, and both are guarded. Flyway runs migrations on plain JDBC, not on JdbcTemplate. The PgJDBC driver's own loggers fall under `org.postgresql`, which is guarded. So in today's code, turning on TRACE for `org.springframework.jdbc` can't log any answers. The finding admits this by pointing at "later slices", which makes it a possible future gap, not a correctness bug in this code. The doc comment says "Hibernate/JDBC bound parameter values", and that is accurate for the binders the app actually uses. Adding `org.springframework.jdbc` would be cheap hardening, but the claimed leak doesn't happen in the current code.

I read the guard at RequestContentLogGuard.kt:34-47. It's true that `org.springframework.jdbc` is not in GUARDED. But nothing in this repo can reach the logger the finding names. I searched `src/**` and `pom.xml` for JdbcTemplate, JdbcClient, NamedParameterJdbc and spring-jdbc and found no matches. `StatementCreatorUtils` only logs parameter values when a JdbcTemplate or JdbcClient binds them. Persistence here goes through Hibernate/JPA, which binds through its own `org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind` logger, and that logger is guarded. Flyway runs append-only DDL with no user-supplied bind values. So no request content can reach an unguarded Spring JDBC logger in the current code. Two more things would have to happen first: an operator would have to set `logging.level.org.springframework.jdbc=TRACE`, and a future slice would have to add JdbcTemplate usage. The finding itself says "including in later slices", which makes this a speculative hardening suggestion rather than a bug that can be reproduced. It's still a reasonable thing to add if a later slice brings in JdbcTemplate, but it can't happen for any user or attacker today.
